intro: Tell me about yourself and why this role.

SDE.question: What is the difference between a process and a thread?
key_points: A process has its own separate memory space
Threads of one process share the same memory
Switching between threads is cheaper than between processes
Shared memory means threads need synchronisation such as locks

SDE.question: How does a hash table work, and what is its time complexity?
key_points: A hash function maps a key to an array index
Average lookup, insert and delete are O(1)
Collisions are handled by chaining or open addressing
Worst case becomes O(n) when many keys collide

SDE.question: What is a deadlock and how can you prevent it?
key_points: Two or more threads wait forever for resources held by each other
Needs mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait
Breaking any one condition prevents deadlock
Acquiring locks in a fixed global order is a common prevention

SDE.question: Explain SQL injection and how to prevent it.
key_points: Attack inserts SQL via unsanitised user input
Parameterised queries prevent injection
ORM and input validation add defence layers

SDE.question: What is indexing in a database?
key_points: Index speeds up reads but slows writes
B-tree is the common index structure
Wrong indexes increase storage and write cost

Data Analyst.question: Explain ETL.
key_points: Extract pulls data from sources
Transform cleans and reshapes the data
Load writes it to the target store

Data Analyst.question: What is SQL window function?
key_points: Runs a calculation across a row set related to the current row
Does not collapse rows like GROUP BY
ROW_NUMBER and RANK are common examples

Data Analyst.question: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING in SQL?
key_points: WHERE filters rows before grouping
HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY
HAVING can use aggregate functions like COUNT or SUM

Data Analyst.question: How would you handle missing values in a dataset?
key_points: First measure how much data is missing and whether there is a pattern
Drop rows or columns when only a small share is missing
Impute with mean, median or mode, or forward fill for time series
Document the choice because it can bias the analysis

Data Analyst.question: When would you use the median instead of the mean?
key_points: The mean is pulled by outliers
The median is robust for skewed data
Income or house prices are typical examples where the median is better

ML Engineer.question: What is overfitting and how do you prevent it?
key_points: The model learns noise in the training data
High training accuracy but low validation or test accuracy
Prevent with more data, regularisation such as L1, L2 or dropout
Use cross-validation, early stopping or a simpler model

ML Engineer.question: Explain the bias-variance trade-off.
key_points: Bias is error from overly simple assumptions and causes underfitting
Variance is sensitivity to the training data and causes overfitting
Reducing one usually increases the other
The goal is the model complexity with the lowest total error

ML Engineer.question: What is the difference between precision and recall?
key_points: Precision is TP divided by TP plus FP
Recall is TP divided by TP plus FN
Improving one often lowers the other
F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall

ML Engineer.question: Why do we split data into training, validation and test sets?
key_points: The training set is used to fit the model parameters
The validation set is used to tune hyperparameters and choose models
The test set gives an unbiased final estimate and is used only once

ML Engineer.question: How does a convolutional neural network work?
key_points: Convolution layers slide small learned filters over the image
Filters share weights, so there are far fewer parameters than a dense network
Pooling layers reduce spatial size
Early layers detect edges and later layers detect complex features

Embedded.question: What is the difference between polling and interrupts?
key_points: Polling repeatedly checks a status flag and wastes CPU time
An interrupt lets hardware signal the CPU when an event happens
The CPU runs an interrupt service routine then returns
ISRs should be short and must not block

Embedded.question: What does the volatile keyword do in C, and when do you use it?
key_points: It tells the compiler the value can change outside normal program flow
The compiler must not optimise away reads or writes
Used for hardware registers and variables shared with an ISR
volatile does not make an operation atomic

Embedded.question: Compare I2C and SPI.
key_points: I2C uses two wires, SDA and SCL, with device addresses
SPI uses MOSI, MISO, SCK and a chip-select line per device
SPI is full duplex and usually faster
I2C needs fewer pins when many devices share the bus

Embedded.question: When would you use an RTOS instead of a bare-metal super loop?
key_points: An RTOS schedules tasks by priority with predictable timing
It provides semaphores, mutexes and queues for task communication
A super loop is simpler with less memory overhead
Use an RTOS when several tasks have different timing deadlines

Embedded.question: What is PWM and where is it used?
key_points: The signal switches on and off at a fixed frequency
Duty cycle is the share of time the signal is on
Duty cycle controls the average voltage or power
Used for motor speed, LED brightness and servo control

Web Developer.question: What is the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
key_points: == performs type coercion before comparison
=== checks both value and type without coercion
NaN === NaN is false

Web Developer.question: What is virtual DOM and why is it used?
key_points: Virtual DOM is a lightweight JS copy of the real DOM
Diffing algorithm minimizes direct DOM mutations
Batch updates reduce reflow/repaint cost

Web Developer.question: Explain event delegation.
key_points: Single listener on parent handles events for children
Uses event bubbling to capture target
Reduces memory usage vs individual listeners

Web Developer.question: What is the difference between let, const, and var?
key_points: var is function-scoped; let/const are block-scoped
const cannot be reassigned
var hoists with undefined; let/const hoist but stay TDZ

Web Developer.question: What is CORS and why does it matter?
key_points: CORS controls which domains can call the API
Browser blocks cross-origin requests by default
Server sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin header
